public_rationale: The claim says generative AI alone is not the way to get agents with common sense, sound reasoning, grounding, reliability and theory of mind. It is a conditional, open-ended view about what can work, with no deadline and no measure. 2025 evidence shows generative-AI agents still failing often and sometimes strangely. That fits the claim, but it cannot show that generative AI will never get there. It is also unclear what 'alone' covers, since real agents add tools and code. No dated evidence can settle the claim.
limitations: The 2025 failures match Marcus's view, but they do not decide a claim that something is impossible.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: If what you want is agents with common sense, sound reasoning, tight grounding in reality, reliable instruction-following and enough theory of mind to infer intentions, generative AI alone is not the ticket, because those are exactly the sticking points that have stymied it over and over again.
conditions: if what you want is agents with the stated capabilities, including inferring intentions

our_interpretation: The claim is conditional on a goal (agents with common sense, reasoning, grounding, reliability and theory of mind). It says generative AI alone cannot reach that goal. It has no deadline and no measure.

The backward-looking part (generative AI has repeatedly struggled on these points) is a broad characterisation. The forward part ('aren't the ticket') is an open-ended statement that something is impossible, which no dated evidence can settle.
criteria.support_condition: Not adjudicable: you cannot observe that generative AI will never meet the goal.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Would be contradicted by a purely generative-AI agent that is broadly shown to have the listed capabilities reliably. No agreed test for that exists.
